title: Bounded unramified points give a finite-type local Néron model
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], $E=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$, and $T=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Choose a geometric point $\bar t$ over the closed point of $T$ [def-weil-geometric-point]. Let $R^{\mathrm{sh}}=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{T,\bar t}$ be its strict henselization [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], and write $E^{\mathrm{sh}}=\operatorname{Frac}(R^{\mathrm{sh}})$. Let $G$ be a smooth separated group scheme of finite type over $E$ [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose $G(E^{\mathrm{sh}})$ is bounded in the following sense. There are finitely many affine opens $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ covering $G$, finite $E$-algebra generating lists $(b_{ij})_j$ for each $B_i$, subsets $C_i\subseteq U_i(E^{\mathrm{sh}})$ whose union is $G(E^{\mathrm{sh}})$, and integers $c_i$, such that $v(b_{ij}(x))\geq c_i$ for every $x\in C_i$ and every $j$. Here $v$ is the discrete valuation of the DVR $R^{\mathrm{sh}}$, with $v(0)=+\infty$. Then there are a smooth separated finite-type $T$-scheme $M$ and an isomorphism $M_E\simeq G$ satisfying the mapping property for every smooth $T$-scheme. The mapping property for a $T$-scheme $M$, equipped with $M_E\simeq G$, means that restriction followed by this isomorphism is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_T(X,M)\to\operatorname{Hom}_E(X_E,G)$ for every smooth $T$-scheme $X$, where $X_E=X\times_T\operatorname{Spec}E$ [def-pc-base-change, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. No completeness, excellence or perfection hypothesis is imposed on $R$.

proof.text: The coordinate lower bounds are precisely the affine-cover boundedness hypothesis of [lem-sfb-bounded-group-translation-model]: no change of valuation or completion is involved. Apply it to obtain a smooth separated finite-type model $Y$ of $G$, with nonempty special fibre and birational extensions of both translations after every $A=\mathcal O_{Z,\xi}$ in its statement. In what follows, dense over $T$ always means dense in each of its two fibres, not merely dense in the total space.

source.place: 1.1 Definition 2; 3.5 Theorem 2; 4.3 Proposition 4(iii); primary online scan read, local copy WANTED

proof.text: Consider $\Phi_E(x,y)=(x,xy)$ and $\Psi_E(x,y)=(xy,y)$ on $G\times_EG$. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-trait-local-rational-spreading] with $Z=Y$ and $V=W=Y\times_TY$, first over the first projection and then over the second. At $A=\mathcal O_{Y,\xi}$ the first coordinate of $\Phi_E$, respectively the second of $\Psi_E$, supplies a point of $G(\operatorname{Frac}A)$, so step 1 gives the required local birational translation. The birational clause of the spreading lemma therefore gives $T$-birational maps $\Phi,\Psi$. Products here are smooth by base change [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2) and composition [lem-trf-smooth-composition]. Set $m=p_2\Phi$ on its domain, and compare with $p_1\Psi$ on their common domain. They agree on the generic fibre and hence agree by the uniqueness clause of the spreading lemma. They define the same $T$-rational multiplication. Both universal translations are therefore those above. Associativity holds wherever both composites are defined: on such an open in $Y^3$ the two morphisms agree on the generic fibre by associativity of $G$, and the same uniqueness clause, with base $Z=T$, makes them equal. Products of the smooth finite-type $Y$ satisfy its hypotheses.

source.place: 4.3 Proposition 5, universal left and right translations; primary online scan read, local copy WANTED

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-trait-birational-group-envelope] to $(Y,m)$. All its hypotheses were established: $Y$ is smooth, separated, of finite type, with nonempty special fibre; $m$ agrees with the full group law on $Y_E=G$; both universal translations are birational over $T$; and associativity holds. Obtain a smooth separated finite-type group scheme $M$ and a $T$-dense open immersion $Y\hookrightarrow M$, identifying $M_E$ with $G$ as group schemes. It remains to establish the mapping property; it is not supplied by the envelope lemma.

source.place: 4.3 Theorem 6 and 5.1 Theorem 5; primary online scan read, local copy WANTED

proof.text: Let $Z$ first be an affine smooth finite-type $T$-scheme and $a_E:Z_E\to G$ any morphism. On the generic fibre define $\tau_E:Z_E\times_EG\to Z_E\times_EG$ by $(z,g)\mapsto(z,a_E(z)g)$. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-trait-local-rational-spreading] with $V=W=Z\times_TM$ over $Z$. For each $\xi\in Z_k$ generic, evaluate $a_E$ at $\operatorname{Spec}\operatorname{Frac}(\mathcal O_{Z,\xi})$. Step 1 extends translation by that point birationally on $Y_A$. Composing its target with $Y_A\hookrightarrow M_A$ gives a morphism on an $A$-dense open of $M_A$, since $Y_A$ is $\operatorname{Spec}A$-dense in $M_A$: the open immersion $Y\hookrightarrow M$ is $T$-dense, and $\operatorname{Spec}A\to T$ sends the closed point to the closed point and the generic point to the generic point, so the base-change clause of [lem-sfb-smooth-trait-local-rational-spreading] applies. Include the full generic fibre, where translation on $G$ is defined; the maps agree on overlaps by generic-fibre uniqueness. The spreading lemma gives a morphism $\tau:D\to Z\times_TM$ on a $T$-dense open $D$ containing $(Z\times_TM)_E$. The source and target over $Z$ are smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2); their composites to $T$ are smooth by [lem-trf-smooth-composition].

source.place: 4.4 Corollary 4, translation by a generic morphism; primary online scan read, local copy WANTED

proof.text: Compose $\tau$ with $p_M$ to get $b:D\to M$. Put $X=Z\times_TM$, smooth over $T$ by step 4, hence flat [lem-pc-smooth-flat] and Noetherian. Every $x\in X$ with $\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}\leq1$ lies in $D$. If $x\in X_E$ this holds as $D\supseteq X_E$; if $x$ is a generic point of $X_k$ it holds as $D_k$ is dense in $X_k$. Otherwise $x\in X_k$ is a proper specialization of a generic point $\eta$ of $X_k$. Since $\mathcal O_{X,\eta}$ is flat over $R$, the uniformizer of $R$ is a nonzerodivisor in its maximal ideal, so it lies in no minimal prime and $\dim\mathcal O_{X,\eta}\geq1$; thus $\eta$ is a proper specialization of a point of $X_E$, and $\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}\geq2$. Also $D$ is dense in both fibres of $X$. Hence [lem-sfb-relative-weil-codimension-extension], with Dedekind domain $R$, base $T$, smooth source $X$, the smooth separated $T$-group $M$, $V=D$ and $u=b$, extends $b$ to $B:Z\times_TM\to M$. With the identity section $e:T\to M$, define $a=B\circ(\operatorname{id}_Z,e\circ p_Z):Z\to M$. On the generic fibre its value is $a_E(z)1=a_E(z)$, so $a$ extends the prescribed map. Notice that the extension theorem is applied to the $T$-group $M$ and the smooth $T$-source $Z\times_TM$, not to a possibly nonsmooth closure or to a group over $Z$.

source.place: 4.4 Theorem 1 and Corollary 4, evaluation along the identity section; primary online scan read, local copy WANTED

proof.text: For any smooth $T$-scheme $Z$, cover it by affine opens $Z_i$ of finite type over $T$; smoothness is locally of finite presentation, by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]. Step 5 produces extensions on each $Z_i$. They agree on overlaps by the uniqueness clause of [lem-sfb-smooth-trait-local-rational-spreading], applied locally with base $T$ and target $M$. Its source may be restricted to affine finite-type opens in each overlap. Thus the extensions glue to a morphism $Z\to M$. The same uniqueness clause shows that two morphisms with the same generic restriction coincide, locally on $Z$ and hence globally. Restriction is therefore both surjective and injective for every smooth $Z$, as required. If $Z_k$ is empty the argument simply uses the given generic-fibre map; the empty source also causes no exception.
